nodes.line: You just flew in, or you just rolled off the freight line. Either way, you just got here — and HQ knew it first.

options.label: Ask about Flock HQ
options.response: The tower watches the whole grid from downtown. Cameras grow faster than peaches around here. Sweeter margins, too.

options.label: Mention the Form 27-B you are definitely not filling in
options.response: Paper moves through this city like humidity. Give it time. It's already somewhere it needs to be.

options.label: Report in after orientation
options.response: HQ keeps its own roster, but word trickles down. You're cleared. The ladder racks are by the freight elevator.

options.label: Ask what the streets are saying
options.response: Same thing they always say, just louder now that the poles have ears. You didn't get that from me.

options.label: Move along
options.response: Stay sweet. The city likes that. It's watching how sweet you stay.

nodes.line: Langley runs it all from up there. 'Community safety,' he calls it. The community feels real safe. Safe and observed.

options.label: Ask about Langley
options.response: Smiles like a neighbor, counts like a census. He'll shake your hand and log your grip strength.

options.label: Drop the subject
options.response: Wise. The tower has long ears and a longer memory.

nodes.line: Back in my day we didn't need cameras. We had neighbors. Nosy, God-fearing neighbors with nothing better to do.

options.label: Ask about his house
options.response: Bought it in '74 for the price of a decent truck. Best decision I ever made. You people buy coffee instead of houses. That's the whole problem.

options.label: Ask about the new cameras
options.response: Love 'em. Caught a raccoon on mine Tuesday. Emailed the footage to the whole homeowners' association. Twice.

options.label: Leave Hank to his porch
options.response: You kids just don't know hard work. My lawn mower is older than you and it starts on the first pull.

nodes.line: Pole 40 needs a unit by Friday. Pole 41 needed one last Friday. The grid doesn't sleep and neither does my crew, apparently.

options.label: Ask about the work
options.response: Ladders, brackets, firmware, repeat. Pay's steady. Steady is all anyone asks for down here.

options.label: Ask about the quota
options.response: HQ wants the whole metro lit by Christmas. I want a sandwich. One of us is getting what we want.

options.label: Leave the crew to it
options.response: Watch for the orange cones. And the lenses. Mostly the lenses.

nodes.line: You hold a ladder straight, you got a job. You ask what the units are for, you got a problem. Simple arrangement.

options.label: Say you can hold a ladder
options.response: Good. Report to any pole with a gold bracket. The ladder remembers your hands. Don't ask how.

options.label: Ask what the units are for
options.response: Safety. Progress. Synergy. Pick whichever one lets you sleep. That's what I do.

nodes.line: Yuh. They put a camera on the block, so I put the block on a track. Stream it everywhere. Can't surveil what you can't mute.

options.label: Ask about the music
options.response: Every verse is a map of the blind spots. You memorize the flow, you know where the lenses ain't. That's distribution.

options.label: Ask about the chain
options.response: It's a camera. Gold-plated. Doesn't work. That's the statement.

options.label: Nod and bounce
options.response: Tell the tower I said the mixtape drops Friday. It already knows. It pre-ordered.

nodes.line: Track four is just me reading the serial numbers off the units on Peachtree. It charted. The tower filed a noise complaint against itself.

options.label: Ask for the blind spots
options.response: I don't hand out the map for free, but listen close to the hook. Everything I know is in the hook.

options.label: Compliment the wordplay
options.response: Yuh. The pen is mightier than the lens. Somebody should write that down. Oh wait. I did. Track six.

name: Mr. Garrett Langley
role: Founder & CEO, Flock — Here to Listen

nodes.line: Hey there. Garrett. Welcome to the home office. I don't do titles — I'm just a neighbor who happens to own the cameras. All of them.

options.label: Ask about Flock's mission
options.response: Simple: we make communities safer. Total visibility is total safety. A watched neighborhood is a loved neighborhood.

options.label: Raise privacy concerns
options.response: I hear that a lot, and I want you to know: I hear it. Because of the microphones. Which I value.

options.label: Ask about working for Flock
options.response: We're always hiring eyes. You look like someone with a lot of neighbors. Ever considered being compensated for that?

options.label: End the conversation
options.response: Great talk. This never happened, but it was great. I'll see you around. Technically, I already am.

nodes.line: People ask me, 'Garrett, isn't this surveillance?' And I say no. Surveillance is what governments do. We're a company. We call it stewardship.

options.label: Point out that it's a distinction without a difference
options.response: Right, but it's a profitable distinction. And profitable means sustainable. Safety shouldn't have to worry about a runway.

options.label: Nod and step back
options.response: I can tell you're a person who gets it. The cameras can too. They flagged you as 'gets it.'

nodes.line: Privacy is important. It's so important we monitor it constantly. If your privacy drops below acceptable levels, we want to be the first to know.

options.label: Ask how to opt out
options.response: Great question. The opt-out form is Form 88-C. It's not distributed, but the act of looking for it tells us you're engaged. We love engagement.

options.label: Withdraw the concern
options.response: No, no, your concern is valid and has been logged. Concerns are data. We treasure your data.

nodes.line: Here's the pitch: you watch your block, we pay you. You're not an informant — you're a Community Safety Partner. The vest is free.

options.label: Express cautious interest
options.response: Love it. Orientation's a formality. We already have your file — consider this the handshake.

options.label: Decline the vest
options.response: The offer stands. It always stands. That's not a threat, it's just good retention design.
